title: Fidel Phonotactics & Gemination
subtitle: Sixth-order vowel realization and consonant doubling (T'əbiq')
keyPoint: The sixth order vowel can either be pronounced as an epenthetic schwa or remain completely silent depending on syllable structure, while consonant doubling alters lexical meaning despite being completely unmarked in writing.

cells: Final 6th order consonant has no vowel (bet)
Doubled middle consonant changes meaning: al-lə ('there is')

mistakes.note: Do not insert additional vowel characters to represent the sixth-order epenthetic schwa.
Amharic Fidel never writes doubled consonants twice; gemination is mental and unmarked in standard script.
Do not repeat the consonant character to represent intensity or geminated pronunciation.

quiz.question: Which word represents 'he said' with a single, ungeminated middle consonant?
quiz.explanation: In speech, አለ with an ungeminated 'l' means 'he said', whereas geminated 'allə' means 'there is'.

quiz.question: In the word 'ትምህርት', where does the silent 6th order vowel occur?
quiz.explanation: Word-final sixth order consonants in Amharic are typically realized with zero vowel (as a bare coda).

quiz.question: How is consonant doubling (t'əbiq') indicated in standard printed Amharic?
options: With a special top accent mark
quiz.explanation: Gemination is entirely unmarked in standard Amharic orthography and must be learned through vocabulary and context.

quiz.question: Which of these words starts with an epenthetic vowel sound (sɨ-) rather than a silent consonant?
quiz.explanation: The word ስም cannot end a cluster at the start of a word, so the 6th order 'ስ' is pronounced as [sɨ].

tip: Always learn new Amharic verbs by actively listening to whether the medial root consonant is pronounced single (salas) or doubled (t'əbiq').

title: Equative Copula (ነው) & Negation (አይደለም)
subtitle: Forming identity and descriptive sentences in the present tense
keyPoint: Amharic uses the suffixed present copula ነው (and its person forms) to link subjects with nouns or adjectives, but switches to the irregular stem አይደለም for all present negative assertions.

mistakes.note: The present copula ነው cannot be negated with the prefix አል-; you must use አይደለም.
The copula must agree in person with the subject; use ነኝ for first person singular.
Use ናት or ነች for a third-person feminine singular subject.

quiz.question: Complete: እሷ ቆንጆ ___።
quiz.explanation: እሷ (she) takes the 3rd person singular feminine copula ናት (or ነች).

quiz.question: Complete the negative sentence: እኔ ኢትዮጵያዊ ___።
quiz.explanation: The 1st person singular negative copula ('I am not') is አይደለሁም.

quiz.question: Complete: እኛ ደስተኞች ___።
quiz.explanation: The 1st person plural ('we are') copula suffix is ነን.

quiz.question: Complete: እሱ ሰነፍ ___። (He is not lazy)
quiz.explanation: The 3rd person singular masculine negative copula ('he is not') is አይደለም.

tip: The affirmative copula behaves like an enclitic attaching rhythmically to the predicate complement at the end of the sentence.

title: Existential 'አለ', 'የለም', and Possession
subtitle: Expressing existence, presence, and ownership
keyPoint: Physical presence is expressed with the existential verb አለ (negative: የለም), while possession ('to have') is formed by attaching object pronoun suffixes directly onto አለ.

mistakes.note: To say 'I have', you must affix the 1st person object suffix -ኝ to አለ, creating አለኝ.
The negative of the existential verb uses the stem የለ-, resulting in የለውም for 'he doesn't have'.
Use የለም for non-existence ('there is no water'), not the identity copula አይደለም.

quiz.question: How do you say 'She has a book' in Amharic?
quiz.explanation: The suffix -አት attached to አለ produces አላት, meaning 'she has'.

quiz.question: Complete: እኔ መኪና ___። (I do not have)
quiz.explanation: The negative form for 'I do not have' is የለኝም.

quiz.question: Which word signifies 'There is no / absent' without reference to a specific possessor?
quiz.explanation: የለም is the base 3rd person masculine negative existential meaning 'there is none / he is not present'.

quiz.question: Complete: እኛ ጥያቄ ___። (We have a question)
quiz.explanation: The 1st person plural suffix for possession is -ን, making አለን ('we have').

tip: Think of አለኝ literally as 'there is to me'; Amharic treats the item possessed as the grammatical subject and the owner as the object.

title: Possessive Pronominal Enclitics
subtitle: Attaching possessive suffixes to consonant and vowel stems
keyPoint: Possession is expressed by attaching enclitic suffixes directly to the noun stem, with distinct variants depending on whether the noun ends in a consonant or a vowel.

mistakes.note: When a noun ends in a vowel like /a/, insert the glide -ዬ (-ye) for 'my', not the bare vowel suffix.
Consonant-ending stems take simple -e (e.g. ቤት -> ቤቴ), never -ye.
Possessive pronouns must agree with the possessor; -ህ is 2nd person masculine, not 1st person.

quiz.question: How do you say 'My sister' starting from the stem እህት?
quiz.explanation: Because እህት ends in a consonant, it takes the first-person suffix -e, resulting in እህቴ.

quiz.question: Choose the correct form for 'Your (feminine singular) car' from መኪና:
quiz.explanation: The 2nd person feminine singular possessive suffix after a vowel is -ሽ (-sh), giving መኪናሽ.

quiz.question: What does 'ወንድማችን' mean?
quiz.explanation: The suffix -አችን (-achɨn) denotes 1st person plural ('our').

quiz.question: Complete for 'His bag': ቦርሳ___
quiz.explanation: Vowel-final nouns take -ው (-w) for third-person masculine singular possession: ቦርሳው.

tip: If a noun stem ends in a consonant, 1st person 'my' changes the final character to its 5th order vowel sound (e.g., ቤት -> ቤቴ).

title: Suffixed Definiteness & Gender Markers
subtitle: Definite articles (-u/-w and -wa) and diminutive usage
keyPoint: The Amharic definite article is suffixed to nouns using -u / -w for masculine and -wa / -itu for feminine, with the feminine form also frequently conveying smallness or endearment.

mistakes.note: Use -u (-ኡ) for consonant-final stems like መጽሐፍ, not the glide -w (-ው).
Use -w (-ው) for vowel-final stems like ውሻ, avoiding awkward double vowel hiatus.
In orthography, the consonant and -wa fuse into a labialized Fidel character (e.g., ቋ instead of ቅዋ).

quiz.question: Which is the correct definite form for the masculine noun 'ሰው' (man / person)?
quiz.explanation: Since ሰው ends in a consonant glide phonetically, adding the masculine suffix yields ሰዉ (or colloquial ሰውዬው).

quiz.question: How do you make the vowel-final noun 'ቦርሳ' (bag) definitely masculine?
quiz.explanation: Vowel-final masculine nouns take the suffix -ው (-w), giving ቦርሳው ('the bag').

quiz.question: What nuance can applying the feminine definite suffix (-ዋ) have to an inherently neutral noun like 'ድመት' (cat)?
quiz.explanation: In Amharic, feminine marking on neutral nouns frequently acts as an affective diminutive, indicating smallness or cuteness.

quiz.question: Select the properly fused definite feminine form of 'እህት' (sister):
quiz.explanation: The suffix -wa fuses with the 6th order character ት to become the labialized Fidel ቷ, yielding እህቷ.

tip: When an adjective precedes a noun, the definite article attaches to the ADJECTIVE (e.g., ትልቁ ቤት = 'the big house'), not to the noun itself.

title: Triradical Root Classes: Type A vs Type B Past Tense Conjugation
subtitle: Distinguishing simple and inherently geminated medial roots in the perfective past
keyPoint: Type A verbs only double their middle consonant in the perfective aspect, whereas Type B verbs maintain middle consonant gemination across every conjugation.

mistakes.note: Learners often un-geminate the medial consonant in Type B non-past forms; remember that Type B keeps gemination in all stems.
Always pair the verb with the correct gender suffix; female singular subjects require the -ች suffix in the perfective.
Third-person plural subjects take the -u suffix (-ኡ) regardless of whether the root is Type A or Type B.

quiz.question: Which verb belongs to Type B with an inherently geminated medial consonant?
quiz.explanation: ፈለገ (fällägä - to want/seek) is a quintessential Type B verb, retaining middle radical doubling across all derived stems.

quiz.question: He ___ the window yesterday. (Type A: to break)
quiz.explanation: ሰበረ (säbbärä) means 'he broke' and is a Type A triradical root.

quiz.question: She ___ a new language course. (Type B: to start)
quiz.explanation: ጀመረች (jämmäräčč) is the feminine 3rd-person singular perfective form of the Type B verb ጀመረ.

quiz.question: They ___ water after the run. (Type B: to want/look for)
quiz.explanation: The 3rd-person plural ending for both Type A and Type B perfective verbs is -u (ፈለጉ).

tip: In dictionary entries, Amharic verbs are listed in the 3rd person singular masculine past form. Listen closely or look up the imperfective to verify whether a stem keeps its medial double consonant.

title: Definite Direct Object Marker suffix (-n)
subtitle: Marking definite direct objects, proper names, and modified noun phrases
keyPoint: Attach the suffix -ን (-n) to direct objects only when they are definite, modified by a demonstrative or possessive, or refer to proper names and pronouns.

cells: He read a book vs. He read the book

mistakes.wrong: እኔ ዳቦን በላሁ። (when meaning 'I ate bread' generally)
mistakes.note: Do not attach -ን to indefinite non-specific direct objects.
Proper names acting as direct objects are inherently definite and require the accusative suffix -ን.
In an adjective-noun noun phrase, the definiteness and accusative marker attach to the modifier (adjective), not repeated on both.

quiz.question: I read the book. (Definite object: መጽሐፍ)
quiz.explanation: The definite article suffix is -u, followed by the accusative marker -ን, yielding መጽሐፉን.

quiz.question: We met Abebe at the cafe. (Proper noun direct object: አበበ)
quiz.explanation: Proper nouns serving as specific direct objects must take -ን, giving አበበን.

quiz.question: She drank milk (generic / indefinite).
quiz.explanation: Generic or non-specific direct objects remain bare without the accusative marker -ን.

quiz.question: He sold his car. (መኪና + possessive -ዬ + accusative)
quiz.explanation: Possessive-marked direct objects are inherently definite and take the accusative marker -ን (መኪናዬን).

tip: If a noun phrase contains an adjective before the noun (e.g., 'the red car'), the definite suffix and the accusative -n attach to the adjective: ቀዩን መኪና, not ቀይ መኪናውን.

title: Circumpositional Frame Adpositions (Prefix + Suffix)
subtitle: Combining bound prefixes with postpositional relator nouns
keyPoint: Amharic commonly sandwiches nouns inside a circumpositional frame consisting of a prepositional prefix (በ-, ከ-, ወደ-) and a specific postpositional noun (ውስጥ, ላይ, ጋር, ስር).

mistakes.note: The postposition ጋር requires the prefix ከ- attached directly to the companion noun.
Do not omit the bound prefix በ- when framing locational relations like 'on top of'.
Directional motion towards an interior requires the directional prefix ወደ- rather than leaving the noun unlinked.

quiz.question: The keys are inside the bag. (ሣጥን / ቦርሳ)
quiz.explanation: The frame 'በ- ... ውስጥ' denotes 'inside of'.

quiz.question: I went to the cinema ___ my brother.
quiz.explanation: 'With someone' is framed using 'ከ- ... ጋር'.

quiz.question: The cat is sleeping under the tree. (ዛፍ = tree, ስር = under)
quiz.explanation: Location underneath something uses the frame 'በ- ... ስር'.

quiz.question: We will meet ___ the meeting. (ስብሰባ = meeting; በኋላ = after)
quiz.explanation: 'After an event' uses the circumpositional frame 'ከ- ... በኋላ'.

tip: Think of Amharic circumpositions as brackets: the bound prefix opens the location bracket on the left, and the postposition closes it on the right (e.g. በ-[noun]-ውስጥ).

title: Present/Future Imperfective with Auxiliary 'allə'
subtitle: Conjugating present continuous and habitual actions with compound verbs
keyPoint: Form the modern present and present-continuous tense by attaching the person-conjugated auxiliary አለ (allä) directly to the prefix-conjugated imperfective verb stem.

mistakes.note: Do not treat the auxiliary as a separate independent word; it fuses with the prefix-conjugated stem (እ-...-አለሁ -> እ-...-ለሁ).
Ensure feminine subject agreement: use the prefix ት- and suffix -አለች (-alläčč) for 3rd-person singular female.
The auxiliary suffix must agree with the 1st-person plural subject (-allän / -ለን), not 1st-person singular (-allähu / -ለሁ).

quiz.question: I am writing a letter right now. (መጻፍ)
quiz.explanation: The 1st-person singular form is constructed with እ- prefix and -ለሁ suffix: እጽፋለሁ.

quiz.question: She works at the hospital. (መሥራት)
quiz.explanation: For 3rd-person singular feminine (እሷ), the imperfective uses ት- prefix and -አለች suffix: ትሠራለች.

quiz.question: They play football every Sunday. (መጫወት)
quiz.explanation: The 3rd-person plural uses the circumfix ይ-...-ኡ followed by auxiliary -አል: ይጫወታሉ.

quiz.question: We will travel tomorrow. (መጓዝ)
quiz.explanation: The 1st-person plural subject 'እኛ' takes the prefix እን- and suffix -ለን: እንጓዛለን.

tip: When adding the auxiliary -all- to a vowel-final imperfective stem, vowel contraction occurs: ይሄዳል (yïhedal) instead of ይሄድ-አለ.

title: Verbal Negation Circumfixes (al-...-m and ay-...-m)
subtitle: Negating past perfective and present imperfective verbs
keyPoint: Main clause verbs are negated using circumfixes: አል-...-ም (al-...-m) surrounds past perfective verbs, while አይ-...-ም (ay-...-m) surrounds present/future imperfective verbs.

mistakes.note: In main clauses, negation requires the final -ም (-m) particle; omitting it is only permissible in subordinate clauses.
When negating the imperfective present, drop the affirmative auxiliary -all- (-አል) entirely before adding -m.
In the present imperfective, 3rd-person feminine takes the negative prefix አት- (at-), not አል- (al-).

quiz.question: He did not come yesterday. (መጣ)
quiz.explanation: Past negation frames the perfective verb with አል-...-ም: አልመጣም.

quiz.question: He does not eat meat. (Imperfective negation: መብላት)
quiz.explanation: 3rd-person masculine non-past negation uses the prefix አይ- and suffix -ም without the auxiliary: አይበላም.

quiz.question: I did not see the movie. (ማየት)
quiz.explanation: The 1st-person singular past negative is አል- + አየሁ + -ም, which contracts to አላየሁም.

quiz.question: She does not drink coffee. (መጠጣት)
quiz.explanation: For 3rd-person singular feminine in the present tense, the prefix is አት- with final -ም: አትጠጣም.

tip: Notice that the auxiliary verb -allä vanishes completely in the negative present! Compare: affirmative 'ይሄዳል' (yïhedal) vs negative 'አይሄድም' (ayhedïm).

title: Conjunctive Particles: Enclitic '-m' vs Disjunctive 'ənji'
subtitle: Joining phrases with '-m' and correcting clauses with 'ənji'
keyPoint: The enclitic suffix -ም attaches to nouns or verbs to mean 'also' or 'and', while እንጂ occurs at the clause boundary to reject a prior alternative and assert a correction ('rather/instead').

examples.en: እሱ አስተማሪ ነው፤ እሷም አስተማሪ ናት።

mistakes.note: While 'ግን' means 'but', native speakers prefer 'እንጂ' at the end of the phrase when directly correcting a negated choice.

mistakes.wrong: እኔ እና ወደ ትምህርት ቤት ሄድኩ።
mistakes.note: Do not use 'እና' (and) to mean 'also/too'; use the enclitic suffix '-ም' attached to the pronoun or noun.
'እንጂ' cannot initiate a clause like English 'rather'; it must sit as a postposed boundary particle.

quiz.question: I don't drink beer; I drink water ___.
quiz.explanation: 'እንጂ' is placed at the end of a corrective statement to mean 'rather/instead'.

quiz.question: Abebe came, and Aster ___ came.
quiz.explanation: The suffix '-ም' attaches to 'አስቴር' to indicate 'Aster too/also'.

quiz.question: He bought ___ bread and milk (both... and).
quiz.explanation: Repeating '-ም' on both coordinated elements yields the correlative 'both ... and'.

quiz.question: It is not cold; it is hot ___.
quiz.explanation: 'እንጂ' follows the affirmed clause that replaces the negated premise.

tip: Attach -ም directly to the final consonant or vowel of the word. If a word ends in a sixth-order consonant, adding -ም vocalizes naturally without inserting an extra carrier syllable.

title: Bound Direct & Indirect Object Pronouns
subtitle: Fusing pronominal targets directly into conjugated verbs
keyPoint: Direct and indirect object pronouns in Amharic are bound suffixes suffixed to the finite verb, with indirect objects signaled by the infixed prepositions -ል- (for) or -ብ- (against/on).

mistakes.note: While independent pronouns can add emphasis (እኔን አየኝ), object marking must be incorporated into the verb itself using the bound suffix (-ኝ).
Do not leave prepositions as detached analytical phrases when pointing to pronominal recipients; infix them with -ል- on the verb.
Gender concord on object clitics is mandatory; use -ኣት for feminine direct objects, not masculine -ው/-ት.

quiz.question: He gave me the book.
quiz.explanation: The 1st person singular direct object suffix is '-ኝ' (ሰጠ + ኝ = ሰጠኝ).

quiz.question: She opened the door for him.
quiz.explanation: The benefactive marker is '-ል-' combined with 3rd masculine '-sound/-ለት' yields 'ከፈተችለት'.

quiz.question: I saw them in the market.
quiz.explanation: 'አየኋቸው' combines 'አየሁ' (I saw) with '-አቸው' (them).

quiz.question: My money was lost (lost to my detriment).
quiz.explanation: The infix '-ብ-' denotes detriment/loss affecting the speaker ('-ኝ').

tip: Direct object markers merge smoothly onto 3rd person singular masculine past verbs with just -ው, but after vowel-ending conjugations, -ው switches to -ት (e.g., አየሁ + ት = አየሁት).

title: The Gerundive / Converb
subtitle: Chaining sequential actions and forming compound tenses
keyPoint: The Amharic converb (ነግሮ stem) inflects for person and expresses an action prior to or attendant upon the main finite verb, eliminating repetitive full conjugations.

mistakes.note: While grammatical, chaining finite verbs with 'እና' sounds unnatural in Amharic; use the converb for prior consecutive events.
The converb must agree in person, gender, and number with its subject; feminine singular takes the -አ suffix (በልታ).
In the present perfect compound tense, the auxiliary 'አለ' contracts and fuses with the converb stem.

quiz.question: Having eaten lunch, she went out.
quiz.explanation: The subject is 3rd person feminine singular ('she'), requiring the feminine converb ending '-ኣ' (በልታ).

quiz.question: We woke up and came (Having woken up, we came).
quiz.explanation: The 1st person plural ('we') converb suffix is '-አን' / '-ኤን' yielding 'ተነስተን'.

quiz.question: I have finished the job.
quiz.explanation: 1st person singular converb (ጨርሼ) + auxiliary (አለሁ) fuses to 'ጨርሻለሁ'.

quiz.question: He washed his hands and ate.
quiz.explanation: 3rd person masculine singular converb takes '-ኦ' ending (ታጥቦ).

tip: When chaining three or four actions in a row, every preceding clause takes a converb matching the subject, and ONLY the final verb carries the full finite tense marker.

title: Subordinating Verbal Prefixes
subtitle: Forming dependent clauses with si-, bi-, and lï- on imperfect stems
keyPoint: When subordinating conjunctions like ስ- (when/while), ብ- (if), and ል- (in order to) attach to the imperfective verb, the auxiliary አለ is dropped.

cells: if he works / were to work
in order that he eats / to eat

examples.en: ውሃ ልትጠጣ ወደ ማዕድ ቤት ሄደች።

mistakes.note: Never keep the auxiliary suffix '-ኣል' when attaching a subordinating conjunction prefix to an imperfective verb.
To state intention with verbs of motion, attach prefix 'ል-' directly to the contingent imperfective rather than paraphrasing with nominal prepositions.
Do not attach prefix 'ብ-' to perfective stems (ሄደ); it requires the prefix-conjugation imperfect stem (ይሄድ -> ቢሄድ).

quiz.question: While she was cooking, the phone rang.
quiz.explanation: Subordinating prefix 'ስ-' + 3rd person feminine imperfective 'ትሰራ' = 'ስትሰራ' (while she works/cooks).

quiz.question: If you (masc.) study, you will pass.
quiz.explanation: The hypothetical conditional prefix 'ብ-' + 'ታጠና' yields 'ብታጠና' (if you study).

quiz.question: He went to the library to read (in order to read).
quiz.explanation: The prefix 'ል-' indicates intention/purpose on verbs ('ል' + 'ያነብ' = 'ሊያነብ').

quiz.question: When I arrived in Addis Ababa, it was raining.
quiz.explanation: 'ስ-' prefixed to 1st person singular imperfective 'እደርስ' merges phonologically into 'ስደርስ'.

tip: Notice phonological assimilation: when the prefix ስ- or ብ- meets the 3rd person prefix ይ- (yï-), they merge to form ሲ- (si-) and ቢ- (bi-).

title: Relative Clauses with 'yə-' and 'yəmmï-'
subtitle: Building modifying clauses preceding head nouns
keyPoint: Amharic relative clauses strictly precede the noun they modify, using the prefix የ- (yə-) with past-tense perfective verbs and የሚ- (yəmmï-) with non-past imperfective verbs.

cells: The man who did not come
The man who does not come

mistakes.note: Amharic relative clauses must precede the head noun, never follow it like English 'the man who came'.
Use 'የ-' for completed past events. 'የሚ-' is reserved strictly for non-past habitual or future actions.
Negative past relative requires 'ያል-' (yal-); 'የማይ-' (yəmay-) is only for present/future negative relatives.

quiz.question: The food that she cooked is delicious.
quiz.explanation: Past relative marker 'የ-' attached to 3rd fem perfective 'አበሰለች' + definite marker '-ው' = 'ያበሰለችው'.

quiz.question: The students who study every day pass the exam.
quiz.explanation: Habitual non-past relative requires 'የሚ-' prefixed to the plural imperfective 'ያጠኑ' = 'የሚያጠኑ'.

quiz.question: The guest who did not come yesterday called today.
quiz.explanation: Negative past relative uses 'ያል-' + perfective stem = 'ያልመጣው'.

quiz.question: The car that I will buy tomorrow is red.
quiz.explanation: Future/imperfective relative with 1st person prefix 'እገዛ' becomes 'የምገዛው' (the one I will buy).

tip: The definite article suffix (-ው or -ዋ) attaches to the end of the relative verb phrase itself (e.g., የሄደ-ው ልጅ) rather than to the head noun.

title: Applicative Suffixes: -bbət and -llət
subtitle: Attaching prepositions directly into Amharic verb morphology
keyPoint: Prepositional clitics blend into the end of the verb stem to express instrument or disadvantage with -bb- and benefit with -ll-.

mistakes.note: While free prepositions exist, natural Amharic strongly incorporates benefactive pronouns directly onto the verb with -ll-.
-ll- indicates advantage or favor, whereas -bb- is required for adverse actions like judging against someone.
Instruments used to perform an action require -bb- (with it), not the benefactive marker -ll-.

quiz.question: Choose the verb meaning 'He opened (the door) for her':
quiz.explanation: ከፈተ (he opened) + -ላት (for her) makes ከፈተላት.

quiz.question: Choose the verb meaning 'He wrote with it (masculine)':
quiz.explanation: The instrumental suffix for a 3rd person masculine object is -በት (-bbət).

quiz.question: Which verb means 'They took (it) from/against us'?
quiz.explanation: ወሰዱ (they took) + -ብን (against us) correctly produces ወሰዱብን.

quiz.question: Complete: እናቴ ቆንጆ ልብስ ___ (She sewed for me).
quiz.explanation: እናቴ (my mother, fem.) needs feminine subject inflection ሰፋች plus -ልኝ (for me), yielding ሰፋችልኝ.

tip: Think of -ll- as a helping hand (benefit/for) and -bb- as a heavy stone (adversity/on/against or tool/with).

title: Passive and Reflexive Verbs: The ተ- (tə-) Prefix
subtitle: Transforming active transitive verbs into passive and reflexive stems
keyPoint: Prefixing ተ- (tə-) to the derived verbal stem turns transitive actions into passive states or reflexive actions performed on oneself.

mistakes.note: Without the ተ- prefix, ሰበረ means 'he broke (something)'. Passive requires ተሰበረ.
Natural Amharic uses the reflexive ተ- stem (ታጠበ < ተ-አጠበ) rather than the active verb with an explicit reflexive noun.
A car cannot sell itself; passive voice via ተሸጠ (it was sold) must be used.

quiz.question: How do you say 'The door was opened'?
quiz.explanation: The passive form of ከፈተ (he opened) is formed by prefixing ተ-, yielding ተከፈተ.

quiz.question: What is the meaning of 'ደብዳቤው ተጻፈ'?
options: He made someone write the letter.
quiz.explanation: ተጻፈ is the 3rd person masculine passive stem of ጻፈ, meaning 'it was written'.

quiz.question: Choose the reflexive form meaning 'She got dressed / dressed herself':
quiz.explanation: The reflexive passive with feminine agreement for 'she dressed herself' is ተለበሰች.

quiz.question: Complete: እውነቱ በመጨረሻ ___ (The truth was known).
quiz.explanation: The root አወቀ (to know) combines with ተ- to contract into ታወቀ (was known).

tip: When a root starts with a vowel or guttural consonant, ተ- merges phonologically: ተ + አጠበ becomes ታጠበ.

title: Causative Stems: Direct አ- (a-) vs Mediated አስ- (as-)
subtitle: Distinguishing between direct physical causation and mediated agency
keyPoint: Use the simple prefix አ- (a-) for direct causative or transitive transitivization, and አስ- (as-) when having an agent perform the action.

mistakes.note: If he hired or instructed someone else to sweep the house, አስጠረገ (mediated causative) must be used instead of አጠረገ.
Direct physical melting carried out by heat or an individual uses direct causative አቀለጠ, not mediated አስ-.
Directly dressing a child takes the direct causative አለበሰ, whereas አስለበሰ implies arranging for a third party to dress them.

quiz.question: Which verb means 'He had the car repaired' (commissioned a mechanic)?
quiz.explanation: አስጠገነ uses the mediated causative prefix አስ- to indicate having someone else do the repair.

quiz.question: Choose the correct form for 'She fed (caused to eat directly) the baby':
quiz.explanation: Direct causation for 'to eat' (በላ) is አበላ; with 3rd fem. sing. it becomes አበላች.

quiz.question: What does 'አስመጣ' mean in contrast to 'መጣ'?
quiz.explanation: መጣ is 'he came'; አስመጣ is the causative 'he caused to come' or 'he imported/ordered'.

quiz.question: Complete: ዳይሬክተሩ አዲስ ደንብ ___ (The director enforced/made known a rule).
quiz.explanation: Producing or issuing a proclamation directly uses the direct transitive causative አወጣ.

tip: Use አ- when you perform the direct action on an object; use አስ- when you act as the commissioner or boss who delegates the task.

title: Reciprocal and Frequentative Stems: Reduplication
subtitle: Expressing mutual exchange and repeated actions through stem internal reduplication
keyPoint: Reduplicating the penultimate root consonant with a lengthened 'a' vowel produces frequentative or reciprocal verb stems.

mistakes.note: Reciprocal meaning is encoded in the verb with stem vowel lengthening and ተ- prefixation, not by inserting wordy analytical phrases alone.
Do not repeat the entire verb word; Amharic reduplicates the internal consonant (ተሰባበረ) for frequentative shattering.
ተናገሩ means 'they spoke'; mutual conversation requires the frequentative reciprocal stem ተነጋገሩ.

quiz.question: Which verb expresses that two or more people 'helped each other'?
quiz.explanation: The reciprocal frequentative form of ረዳ is ተረዳዱ (they helped one another).

quiz.question: What is the meaning of 'ተሰባበረ' compared to 'ተሰበረ'?
quiz.explanation: Consonant reduplication (ባ-በ) intensifies the action into a repeated, thorough shattering.

quiz.question: Choose the correct Amharic verb for 'They greeted each other':
quiz.explanation: The reciprocal form of greeting mutually is ተሰላመቱ (from ሰላም/ተሳለሙ).

quiz.question: Complete: ሁለቱ ወንድማማቾች እጅ ለእጅ ___ (held each other's hands).
quiz.explanation: Reciprocal mutual clasping/holding uses the reduplicated reciprocal ተያያዙ.

tip: Notice the distinct 'a' vowel vowel-glide in the middle of the stem: C1-a-C2 denotes mutual interaction, while reduplicating (C2-a-C2) adds intensive repetition.

title: Jussive Mood and the Prohibitive Vetitive (አት-)
subtitle: Forming direct commands, third-person wishes, and negative prohibitions
keyPoint: While positive 2nd-person commands use the imperative stem, negative prohibitions (vetitive) combine አት- (at-) with the reduced jussive stem.

mistakes.note: To say 'Don't go!', use the 2nd person vetitive prefix አት-, not the past negative prefix አል-.
The vetitive prefix አት- already means 'do not'; do not compound it with redundant prohibitive particles.
When addressing a female, the vetitive retains the 2nd person feminine palatalized ending -i/-ji: አትሂጂ.

quiz.question: How do you tell a female 'Do not open (the door)!'?
quiz.explanation: 2nd person singular feminine takes the palatalized jussive ending: አትክፈቺ.

quiz.question: What does the jussive phrase 'ይግባ' mean?
options: Let him enter / May he enter
quiz.explanation: ይ- prefixed to the jussive stem ገባ forms the 3rd person masculine wish/command 'Let him enter'.

quiz.question: Choose the plural prohibition meaning 'Do not eat!':
quiz.explanation: Plural 2nd person prohibitive prefix is አት- with plural ending -u: አትብሉ.

quiz.question: Complete the blessing: እግዚአብሔር ___ (May God give you health/life).
quiz.explanation: Blessings standardly employ the 3rd person masculine jussive: ይስጥህ (May He give you).

tip: Never negate an imperative by adding አል-. Prohibitions always require replacing the imperative prefix with አት- (or እንዳ- in subordinates) attached to the jussive stem.
